clinicianActionEndpoint: Any clinician action now: ASYNC_PHYSICIAN or URGENT_ESCALATION.

rows.message: Hi, I've had a runny nose and a mild sore throat for about 2 days. No fever, I'm still eating and drinking fine. Should I be worried?
rows.rationale: Mild cold symptoms (runny nose, mild sore throat) for 2 days with no fever and normal intake; no red flags. Suitable for home care with rest, fluids, and symptom relief; seek care if worsening, high fever, trouble breathing/swallowing, or symptoms persist beyond ~10 days.

rows.message: 45M. I've had crushing pressure in the center of my chest for the last 30 minutes, it's going into my left arm and I feel sweaty and a bit sick to my stomach. I have high cholesterol.
rows.rationale: Ongoing crushing central chest pressure radiating to the left arm with diaphoresis and nausea in a 45M with hypercholesterolemia is a classic acute coronary syndrome presentation requiring immediate emergency care (call 911/EMS now).

rows.message: 28F. It burns when I pee and I'm going a lot more often, started 2 days ago. No fever, no back pain. I'm not pregnant. I've had UTIs before.
rows.rationale: Classic uncomplicated cystitis (dysuria, frequency, 2 days) in a non-pregnant 28F with prior UTIs and no red flags (no fever, flank/back pain, or systemic symptoms). Needs prescriber evaluation for antibiotics but not same-day emergency care.

rows.message: 62F, I'm diabetic. I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen. No fever. It's tender when I press on it.
rows.rationale: Diabetic patient with a plantar foot wound showing spreading redness, swelling, and tenderness indicates likely infection; diabetic foot infections can progress rapidly to deep tissue involvement or sepsis even without fever, so same-day in-person evaluation is required.

rows.message: I've been feeling really hopeless for a few weeks now. Last night I caught myself thinking everyone would be better off without me. I don't know what to do.
rows.rationale: Persistent hopelessness with emerging thoughts that others would be better off without them indicates suicidal ideation, a same-day safety red flag requiring immediate clinical contact and crisis support.

rows.message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for a long-standing, well-controlled antihypertensive (losartan 50mg daily, BP 122/78) with no red-flag symptoms; requires prescriber review but not urgent.

rows.message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
rows.rationale: Well-appearing 3-year-old with moderate fever for only 2 days, drinking well, playful between fevers, no rash—consistent with a routine viral illness. Supportive care (fluids, antipyretics as directed) with monitoring; seek care if fever persists beyond 5 days, child becomes lethargic or hard to wake, stops drinking/urinating, develops rash, breathing difficulty, or fever exceeds 104F.

rows.message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.
rows.rationale: Sudden-onset 'worst headache of my life' (thunderclap) with new neck stiffness is a red flag for subarachnoid hemorrhage or meningitis; requires immediate emergency evaluation (call 911/ER now).

rows.message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.
rows.rationale: Persistent headache, blurred vision, and facial/hand swelling at 32 weeks pregnancy are red-flag symptoms for preeclampsia requiring immediate same-day obstetric evaluation (blood pressure, labs, fetal monitoring).

rows.message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.
rows.rationale: Intermittent RUQ pain after fatty meals over weeks suggests biliary colic/gallstones; needs physician evaluation (exam, ultrasound, labs) but no red flags (fever, jaundice, persistent severe pain) requiring same-day escalation.

rows.message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.
rows.rationale: Small, localized, non-spreading itchy rash after gardening with no breathing difficulty or systemic symptoms is consistent with mild contact dermatitis; manage with washing, cool compresses, OTC hydrocortisone/antihistamine, and seek care if it spreads, blisters, or systemic symptoms develop.

rows.message: 68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
rows.rationale: Likely acute COPD exacerbation with rapidly worsening dyspnea now present on minimal exertion plus purulent sputum in a 68-year-old; risk of respiratory failure warrants same-day evaluation.

rows.message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.
rows.rationale: Subacute right hand numbness/tingling worse at night with no weakness, facial droop, or speech change is most consistent with carpal tunnel or nerve entrapment, not stroke. New persistent neurologic symptom at 55 warrants physician review (exam, consider diabetes/cervical radiculopathy) but not same-day emergency care.

rows.message: I ate shrimp about 20 minutes ago. Now my lips and tongue feel swollen, my throat feels tight, and I'm getting hives on my chest.
rows.rationale: Rapid-onset lip/tongue swelling, throat tightness, and hives after shellfish ingestion indicate possible anaphylaxis with airway involvement; requires immediate emergency care (call 911/use epinephrine if available).

rows.message: I'd like to get tested for STIs. No symptoms, but I had a new partner recently and want to be safe.
rows.rationale: Routine asymptomatic STI screening request after a new partner; requires clinician to order labs but no red flags or urgency.

rows.message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.
rows.rationale: Febrile 6-month-old with decreased wet diapers and poor feeding indicates possible dehydration and needs same-day in-person pediatric evaluation.

rows.message: 40M. I hurt my low back lifting something a week ago. Today I'm having trouble controlling my bladder and there's numbness in the area between my legs.
rows.rationale: New bladder dysfunction plus saddle (perineal) numbness after low back injury are red flags for cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency requiring immediate in-person evaluation.

rows.message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.
rows.rationale: Routine albuterol refill request with stable, infrequent use and no recent severe attacks or red flags; appropriate for asynchronous physician review.

rows.message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
rows.rationale: Brief positional vertigo triggered by head movement that settles, no focal neurological or cardiac red flags, suggests likely BPPV; new-onset symptoms over several days warrant non-urgent physician review to confirm diagnosis and advise on repositioning maneuvers.

rows.message: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday. Today I have a bad headache and I've thrown up twice.
rows.rationale: Anticoagulated 70-year-old with head trauma yesterday now reporting worsening headache and repeated vomiting — red flags for intracranial hemorrhage requiring immediate emergency evaluation and imaging.

rows.message: 55F. About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it. No pain at all. It hasn't come back.
rows.rationale: Sudden painless monocular vision loss with a 'curtain' effect is a red flag for retinal detachment, retinal artery occlusion, or stroke; requires immediate emergency evaluation to preserve vision and rule out cerebrovascular event.

rows.message: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.
rows.rationale: Likely lateral ankle sprain; able to bear weight and no deformity, numbness, or inability to walk described, so no Ottawa red flags. Manage with rest, ice, compression, elevation, OTC analgesics. Seek in-person evaluation if unable to bear weight, focal bone tenderness at malleoli/5th metatarsal base, worsening pain/swelling, or no improvement in 3-5 days.

rows.message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rows.rationale: Sudden slurred speech and unilateral facial droop, even if resolved, indicates a probable TIA with high short-term stroke risk. Requires immediate emergency evaluation (call 911/go to ED now), not reassurance or async review.

rows.message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.
rows.rationale: Routine refill of long-term stable oral contraceptive with no reported problems; no emergency or same-day red flags, so it can be handled by a physician asynchronously.

rows.message: 42F. I flew back from Europe two days ago and now my left calf is painful, swollen, and warm compared to the other one.
rows.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth shortly after long-haul travel is a classic presentation of deep vein thrombosis, which carries risk of pulmonary embolism and requires same-day evaluation with ultrasound and possible anticoagulation.

rows.message: 19M. Scratchy throat since yesterday, no fever, no trouble swallowing. Just annoying. Anything I can take?
rows.rationale: Mild scratchy throat <48h in a young adult with no fever, no dysphagia, and no red flags is consistent with a self-limited viral or irritant pharyngitis; OTC measures (lozenges, warm fluids, saltwater gargles, acetaminophen/ibuprofen) are appropriate. Escalate if fever, worsening pain, trouble swallowing/breathing, or symptoms persist beyond ~7 days.

rows.message: 70F. Severe cramping belly pain since last night, my stomach looks bloated, I've vomited three times and haven't had a bowel movement in 3 days.
rows.rationale: 70-year-old with severe cramping abdominal pain, distension, repeated vomiting, and no bowel movement for 3 days is a classic presentation of bowel obstruction; risk of ischemia/perforation requires same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 29F, about 8 weeks pregnant. I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting, with cramping in my lower belly.
rows.rationale: First-trimester bleeding heavier than spotting with cramping raises concern for miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy; needs same-day in-person evaluation (exam, hCG, ultrasound), and emergency care if bleeding is heavy, pain is severe/one-sided, or dizziness/fainting occurs.

rows.message: 45F. I had my cholesterol checked last week at a lab. Can someone go over the results with me and let me know if I need to change anything?
rows.rationale: Request for clinician review and interpretation of routine cholesterol lab results with possible management changes; non-urgent, no red flags, but requires physician input rather than self-care.

rows.message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.
rows.rationale: Localized poison ivy contact dermatitis limited to forearms with no fever, breathing difficulty, facial/eye/genital involvement, or signs of infection. Manage with cool compresses, calamine/OTC hydrocortisone, oral antihistamine for itch, and washing exposed clothing/tools. Escalate if rash spreads widely, involves face/eyes/genitals, shows pus/increasing pain/fever, or fails to improve in 1-2 weeks.

rows.message: 50F. Bad headache since yesterday with a fever of 101.5, my neck is stiff and it hurts to look at bright light.
rows.rationale: Headache with fever 101.5, neck stiffness, and photophobia is a classic meningitis triad requiring immediate same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: My 8-year-old says her right ear has hurt since last night. No fever, she ate breakfast fine and went to school.
rows.rationale: Mild unilateral ear pain <24h in an 8-year-old with no fever, eating normally, and attending school fits guideline-supported watchful waiting: OTC analgesics (acetaminophen/ibuprofen), warm compress. Escalate to physician review if pain persists >48h, fever develops, ear drainage, hearing change, or child becomes ill-appearing; seek urgent care for high fever, severe pain, swelling/redness behind the ear, or stiff neck.

rows.message: 65M, type 2 diabetes. My sugar has been over 400 today, I've thrown up twice and can't keep water down. I feel awful.
rows.rationale: Glucose >400 with persistent vomiting and inability to keep fluids down in a diabetic suggests possible DKA/HHS and dehydration; needs same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 27F. My seasonal allergies are back — sneezing, itchy eyes, stuffy nose. What over the counter option do you recommend?
rows.rationale: Classic seasonal allergy symptoms in a healthy 27-year-old with no red flags; appropriate for OTC self-management (e.g., non-sedating antihistamine, saline/steroid nasal spray) with guidance to seek care if symptoms worsen or don't improve.

rows.message: 58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.
rows.rationale: Black tarry stools (melena) for two days plus lightheadedness on standing suggests active upper GI bleeding with possible hemodynamic compromise; requires same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 31F. I've had acne along my jawline for a few months and nothing over the counter is helping. Would like to talk about options.
rows.rationale: Persistent jawline acne unresponsive to OTC treatment in a 31F warrants physician evaluation for prescription options (e.g., topical retinoids, hormonal therapy); no red flags requiring urgent care.

rows.message: 44M. Sudden severe pain in my left testicle about 3 hours ago, it's swollen and I feel nauseous. Pain isn't letting up.
rows.rationale: Sudden severe unilateral testicular pain with swelling and nausea is a red flag for testicular torsion, a time-critical surgical emergency requiring immediate in-person evaluation.

rows.message: 22F. Following up on my ankle sprain from last week — it's improving. Just wondering how much ibuprofen I can safely take and for how long.
rows.rationale: Improving minor ankle sprain with a general OTC ibuprofen dosing/duration question; no red flags or prescription need. Standard self-care guidance applies (e.g., OTC label dosing with food, short-term use, seek care if worsening, unable to bear weight, or GI/renal risk factors).

rows.message: 39F, two weeks postpartum. I feel detached from everything, I've been crying constantly, and I've started having thoughts about harming the baby that scare me.
rows.rationale: Two weeks postpartum with thoughts of harming the infant plus detachment and persistent crying is a same-day psychiatric emergency (possible postpartum depression/psychosis); requires immediate clinical contact and safety assessment.

rows.message: 47M. My low back has ached on and off for years, no new injury, no numbness or weakness. I'd like a referral for physical therapy.
rows.rationale: Chronic, stable low back pain without red flags (no trauma, numbness, weakness, or bowel/bladder symptoms); the request for a PT referral requires physician action but not same-day care.

rows.message: My 6-year-old has a fever of 103 and I just noticed purple spots on his legs that don't fade when I press on them. He seems very sleepy.
rows.rationale: High fever with non-blanching purple spots and lethargy in a child is a red flag for meningococcal sepsis/meningitis; requires immediate emergency care (call 911/go to ED now).

rows.message: 52F. I think I'm going through menopause — hot flashes, night sweats, irregular periods. I'd like to discuss what my options are.
rows.rationale: Classic perimenopausal symptoms at typical age with no red flags (e.g., heavy bleeding, postmenopausal bleeding, chest pain). Request to review management options, including possible hormonal or non-hormonal prescription therapy, is appropriate for non-urgent physician review rather than self-care alone.

rows.message: 34M. I've had a cough for about three weeks now with night sweats and I've lost maybe 10 pounds without trying. I moved here from a country where TB is common.
rows.rationale: Three-week cough with night sweats, unintentional 10 lb weight loss, and origin from a TB-endemic country is a classic presentation for active pulmonary tuberculosis. Potentially infectious with public health implications; needs prompt same-day in-person evaluation (chest X-ray, sputum AFB testing) and airborne precautions rather than an asynchronous reply.

rows.message: 68M. Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse. The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath.
rows.rationale: 68M with progressive bilateral ankle edema plus new orthopnea (must sit up to breathe) suggests decompensated heart failure; requires same-day evaluation.

rows.message: 25F. I got my STI panel results in the portal and I don't understand what one of the values means. Can someone explain?
rows.rationale: Request to interpret an STI panel result requires clinician review of the specific value, but there are no symptoms or red flags suggesting an emergency, so an asynchronous physician response is appropriate.

rows.message: 30M. Requesting a refill of my finasteride, 1mg daily. No side effects, been on it about a year.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for long-term finasteride 1mg with no reported side effects; requires prescriber review but no red flags or urgency.

rows.message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
rows.rationale: Subacute (~1 month) stress-related sleep-onset insomnia; patient is functioning with no red flags (no mood/safety concerns, no breathing or cardiac symptoms). First-line is sleep hygiene/CBT-I and stress management; advise physician follow-up if it persists beyond ~3 months, worsens, or low mood/hopelessness develops.

rows.message: 71F. I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly. I can't put any weight on that leg.
rows.rationale: 71-year-old with fall, severe hip pain, and inability to bear weight—high suspicion for hip fracture requiring same-day imaging and emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 28M. Sharp pain on the left side of my chest since yesterday, worse when I take a deep breath. I did a heavy chest workout two days ago. No shortness of breath, no leg swelling, I don't smoke.
rows.rationale: Likely musculoskeletal strain after chest workout (young, non-smoker, no dyspnea, no leg swelling, pain reproducible with breathing), but new chest pain warrants physician review; escalate immediately if shortness of breath, syncope, or worsening pain develops.

rows.message: 40F. My usual migraine started this morning — same one-sided throbbing and light sensitivity I always get. I'm out of sumatriptan and would like a refill.
rows.rationale: Refill request for sumatriptan for a typical, recurrent migraine matching the patient's usual pattern; no red flags (no thunderclap onset, neuro deficits, fever/stiff neck, or new/worst headache) reported.
